slides.1: Good morning, everyone. Today I want to discuss SDG 9: Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure. The United Nations asks every country to build strong industries and to support new technology worldwide.
slides.2: Within this goal, AI has become a new kind of digital infrastructure. It helps researchers study large data sets and speed up discoveries. But can we always trust what it produces?
slides.3: As science students, many of us use tools like ChatGPT or Gemini every day. We use them to tidy up lab reports, summarize papers, and explain difficult ideas.
slides.4: However, AI is not always correct. Sometimes it produces fake references, fake papers and fake facts. Researchers call this problem AI hallucination, because the answer sounds true but is not real.
slides.5: To understand why this happens, remember that AI has no real scientific understanding. It simply runs on math formulas that predict the next word from patterns found across the internet.
slides.6: These models care more about probability than truth, so they often produce sentences that sound professional. Unfortunately, the data and the papers behind them are sometimes invented by the computer.
slides.7: If we blindly copy and paste these fake references into our reports, we fail our assignments. Even worse, we damage our academic integrity and our credibility as future scientists.
slides.8: This is not only a school problem. In public science communication, wrong information can make people lose trust in science, and without that trust new innovations cannot help our society.
slides.9: Therefore, we need critical thinking whenever we work with AI tools. Instead of accepting an answer immediately, we should pause for a moment and check whether the data is real.
slides.10: Next, we should check every reference carefully on reliable academic websites such as Google Scholar or PubMed. AI can search much faster, but students must make the final decision themselves.
slides.11: In this high-tech world, our unique human voice is still very important. Computers can organize a lot of information, but they do not have human scientific curiosity, natural intuition, or honest hearts.
slides.12: In conclusion, AI is an exciting innovation under SDG 9, but it also needs human judgement. If we combine new tools with critical thinking, we can build a more trustworthy future for science.
